blocking_issues: experiments/transfer_cube/diagnosis.md, Tracking number: 'So a real aim error exists in at least 80 of the 126, and the honest separation for aim is about 0.90.' The evidence does not support this count. 80 is the size of the clean subset (grasp failures whose active chunk was decided before any right-finger contact). It is not the number of failures with an abnormal aim error. An aim AUC of 0.898 (80 failures against 734 successes) means the two groups overlap, and no per-episode count is reported. The clean subset also only rules out the network reacting to the bump. Aim error is still the measured gripper position at the first close, and in this subset that is usually long after first contact. Raw clean rows in design_default.jsonl include t_touch/t_rclose of 101/159, 124/185 and 123/192. So a finger pressing on the cube could hold the arm up or deflect it. Many failing reach_rel z values are 0.076 to 0.087 against a reference of 0.054, which such contact could produce, and nothing in the diagnosis excludes it. The same gap affects 'the typical miss is about 1 cm past what still works'. That is a failure median minus a success p90 of reach error, which this section itself says is partly the bump (the untouched-cube aim medians are 3.6 cm against 1.1 cm), and no tolerance was measured. Evidence that would settle it: the number of clean-subset grasp failures above the success p90 and p95 of aim error, plus the same comparison on a contact-free quantity (commanded joint targets at the close through forward kinematics, or gripper position before first contact at a matched phase). Otherwise reword both sentences to what is shown.

experiments/transfer_cube/diagnosis.md, Near-miss evidence, third bullet: 'Failures sit next to successes ... 34% of failures have a succeeding nearest neighbour.' The numbers say the opposite. Given a failure, the nearest seed also fails 65.8% of the time, against an 18.4% base rate (stage1_stats.json, neighbours). A randomly placed neighbour would succeed about 82% of the time, so 34% is far below chance. This shows strong clustering, which supports the zone reading. It is not evidence that failures border successes or are near misses, yet it is listed as such in the section that must carry the near-miss claim. Evidence that would settle it: restate it as clustering with the base rate beside it, or remove it, and let the near-miss case rest only on measures that bear on it.

Smaller observations:
- Tracking number is uneven inside the target. By my hand calculation from reach_rel and the reference vector, about 13 of the 23 class-0 episodes fall under the success p90 (2.10 cm). The reported 80% above p90 implies about 12 of the other 103 do. Reporting separation per class would be fair.
- Zone description: the y below 0.44 strip is concentrated at x 0.08 to 0.16. By 4 cm cells the bottom row fails 20%, 19%, 68%, 55%, 19%. From raw rows, x 0.08 to 0.16 with y 0.40 to 0.48 has 77 failures in 159 seeds (48%), or 42% of all failures. The diagnosis names only the strip. The per-cell arrows in reach_error.png point toward the centre in most corner cells, so a centre-pull component is visible, and it is fair to call that pattern weak rather than refuted.
- The pre-touch cube shift bullet is close to true by construction (a cube cannot move before it is touched), so it is a sanity check and adds little near-miss evidence.
- failure_map.png shows the agent's two kinds, not SPEC's classes as step 3 asks.
